To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) pregnant women infected with Zika virus (ZikV) in Barcelona (Spain), despite some knowledge gaps, showed good awareness of ZikV and its consequences; 2) they suffered from anxiety, depression and fear due to potential effects on their babies; 3) they perceived stigma and discrimination in the community, and they were afraid to disclose their condition; and 4) their main sources of support came from their partners, relatives and health professionals.

the epidemic of the Zika virus in Spain caused a significant health and emotional burden for migrant women, who suffered from anxiety, depression, fear of stigma and social exclusion.

the social and emotional consequences of the ZIKV outbreak in Spain and the impact on pregnant women, and the role of health professionals in the response to this public health emergency.
